item.title: Closure isn't the end for Antique Kitchen as employees rally with original owner to reopen
item.description: The employees of Antique Kitchen in Portage wouldn't just sit idly by as the owners closed the doors of the decades-old restaurant.

item.title: Have tariffs affected the cost of flowers, chocolate ahead of Valentine's Day?
item.description: With Valentine's Day quickly approaching, local florists and chocolatiers across West Michigan are preparing for one of their busiest weeks of the year. But with many flowers and chocolate coming from overseas, higher costs are adding pressure.

item.title: Kent County group looking for volunteers to support kids in foster care
item.description: CASA of Kent County is running a “phone a friend” campaign this month, looking for volunteers who want to be a consistent, trusted voice for children who have experienced abuse in the foster care system.

item.title: 2 hurt in rear-end crash near Dowagiac, deputies say
item.description: Two people were taken to the hospital after a rear-end crash near Dowagiac Wednesday morning, deputies said.

item.description: MILAN (AP) — Laurence Fournier Beaudry and Guillaume Cizeron arrived at the Milan Cortina Olympics amid a swirl of controversy, with the French ice dancers hoping to upset the dominant American duo of Madison Chock and Evan Bates when it mattered most. item.title: 'Poster child' for congenital heart defects perfectly healthy at 9
item.description: Every year, 40,000 babies are born with congenital heart defects. When Jack Stonex was born nine years ago, he was one of them.

item.title: West Michigan bars prepare for Tigers TV shakeup
item.description: Ilitch Sports and Entertainment announced a new partnership this week with Major League Baseball to air Tigers and Red Wings games as its current partner Main Stream Sports and outlet FanDuel Sports Network continues to struggle financially.

item.title: British TikTok star Josh Clark says Michigan hospital workers accessed his info
item.description: British internet celebrity Josh Clarke says hospital employees accessed his personal information when he was injured during his trip to Michigan.

item.title: 57 years later, double murderer will go free
item.description: Nearly 60 years after murdering two gas station clerks in Walker, a 78-year-old man will go free.

item.title: Whitmer recommends higher taxes for smokers, gamblers and digital ads to plug gap left by Medicaid and SNAP cuts
item.description: Governor Gretchen Whitmer has proposed an $88.1 billion budget for FY 2027 that includes tax increases on tobacco, vaping, internet gaming, sports betting, and digital advertising, as well as targeted tax relief for seniors and low-income families, in order to shield Medicaid, boost literacy, and cut costs for seniors and families.
